title: marketplace-i18n-accessibility-preflight
content:
Purpose
This preflight doc consolidates accessibility (WCAG) and internationalization (i18n) requirements for cloud marketplace listings (AWS, Azure, GCP). Goal: reduce iterative rejections, speed launch, and ensure consistent availability and legal/compliance coverage across regions.

Scope
- Applies to new or updated marketplace listings: product page copy, assets (screenshots, videos), short descriptions, legal blurbs, pricing metadata, and trial/billing flows.
- Excludes internal admin-only landing pages and customer docs (those are covered by Docs i18n team).

Quick acceptance gates (high level)
1) Copy length and field limits verified per marketplace (headline, summary, long description).
2) Alt text present for all screenshots and every image; video transcripts uploaded.
3) Translations for target locales included (see required locales below).
4) WCAG 2.1 AA checks for images, color contrast callouts on screenshots, and keyboard/navigation guidance for demo videos.
5) Privacy/data residency callouts present and aligned with Private offering (if claiming VPC/on-prem).
6) Pricing SKUs and billing mapping verified with Finance (sku mapping doc linked).

Detailed checklist
A. Copy and character limits (marketplace-specific)
- AWS: short description <= 200 chars; long description <= 20,000 chars. Use first 120 chars to convey core value.
- Azure: tagline <= 80 chars; description blocks must avoid markup that Azure strips.
- GCP: summary <= 300 chars; ensure JSON manifest fields match UI copy.
Action: add a small CSV with final character counts next to each copy block.

B. Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA minimum)
- Images/screenshots: every image must have succinct alt text (1–2 short sentences). Mark decorative images explicitly as decorative in alt text field per marketplace format.
- Videos: provide closed captions and a plain-text transcript file. Include keyboard interaction notes for demo flows (what keys to press, focus order).
- Contrast: call out any text overlay on screenshots with a contrast ratio check (WCAG tool screenshot + ratio). If ratio < 4.5:1 for body text, create an alternate screenshot or redesign.
- Keyboard/Focus: if demo uses a modal or keyboard shortcuts, include an accessibility note describing focus trap and how screen-reader users encounter the flow.
Action: engineering to run axe-core on demo UI and save report as artifact.

C. Internationalization (i18n) and localization (l10n)
- Required locales for initial launches: en-US, en-GB, fr-FR, de-DE, es-ES, ja-JP. Additional locales negotiable per region-specific launches.
- Copy tone variants: provide TL;DR (for short description), friendly developer-focused (for long description), and compliance/legal blurb (for legal page).
- Variables/Placeholders: ensure no inline code or template tokens remain (e.g., {{region}}) in final copy.
- Date/number formatting: any example timestamps in copy should be neutral (ISO) or localized in each translation.
- Directionality: verify for RTL locales if added later.
Action: attach translation CSV and request vendor quote; include review turnaround in timeline.

D. Metadata and tags
- Provide 8–12 suggested tags: devops, inference, low-latency, embeddings, private-deployments, gpu-optimized, dedicated-capacity, compliance. Marketplaces often limit tags — prioritize top 5.
- Category mapping: suggest primary category and two secondary categories per marketplace (e.g., AI & ML -> Inference -> Model Serving).

E. Legal / privacy / security copy
- Data residency: if offering Private/VPC, include a short sentence "Data processed in customer-designated region; no persistent storage of customer prompts." Align with Security/Compliance team before publishing.
- KMS/HSM: mention supported KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS) only if validated by infra.
- SLA: marketplace pages often show uptime/SLA blurbs; use conservative language: "SLA available for Dedicated customers" and link to plan details.

F. Assets (images, videos, docs)
- Primary hero screenshot: 16:9 PNG, annotated arrows limited to 3 callouts; provide alt text and a brief caption.
- Secondary screenshots: show console/SDK call, latency graphs, cost breakdowns. Ensure any PII/anonymized data.
- Video: under 90s, captions burned-in AND separate SRT file. Provide a plain-text summary for accessibility.

G. Billing and SKU mapping
- Provide list of SKUs for each offering (Hosted API, Dedicated reserved, Private platform license). Include unit definitions and billing cadence (per-token, monthly reserved capacity, annual license).
- Link finance mapping and required approval gate.

H. Operational readiness and support signals
- Support contact: primary email for trials and a separate escalation path for enterprise.
- Onboarding docs: link to quickstart and sample SDK code in each locale (code not translated, but comments may be localized).
- Trial limits: explicit trial quotas and expiration language.

Copy suggestions (short, medium, legal)
- Short (headline for search): "High‑throughput LLM inference — predictable latency, lower cost."
- Medium (summary for marketplace listing): "Redwood Inference gives engineering teams a unified runtime for serving open and fine‑tuned LLMs across hosted, reserved, and private deployments. Get predictable latency, transparent cost controls, and enterprise-grade controls for regulated data."
- Legal blurb (one sentence): "Use subject to Redwood Inference terms; data handling and residency options available for Dedicated and Private plans."

Acceptance workflow and owners
- Owner: Priya Kapoor (go-to-market) — overall sign-off for copy.
- Accessibility owner: Maya Singh (UX) — signs off WCAG artifacts.
- i18n lead: Evan Burke — coordinates translations.
- Security/Compliance reviewer: add Security team reviewer and obtain written approval for any KMS/residency claims.
Gates: content locked -> accessibility artifacts attached -> translations completed -> legal & finance sign-off -> upload to marketplace portal.

Timeline (example for a single-market launch)
- Day 0: copy freeze
- Day 1–3: accessibility testing + generate artifacts
- Day 4–7: translation vendor turnaround (for required locales)
- Day 8: legal + finance sign-off
- Day 9–10: upload and validate marketplace portal fields

Open questions / TODOs
- Confirm required locale list for APAC launch (include ko-KR, zh-CN?)
- Who provides the final latency/benchmark screenshots? (Ask benchmarks team, ticket BENCH-210)
- Confirm whether marketplace video hosting restrictions require vendor-hosted video or marketplace-hosted links.

Appendix: artifacts to attach on final upload
- CSV with copy fields and character counts per marketplace
- Alt-text spreadsheet matching image file names
- Accessibility test reports (axe-core / manual notes)
- Video SRTs and transcripts
- Translation CSV and vendor acceptance confirmation
- Billing SKU spreadsheet and finance sign-off

Notes: keep copy concise and developer-focused; avoid marketing hyperbole in technical fields. This doc is intentionally pragmatic — add to it as we discover marketplace-specific quirks during each portal upload.
